answer: Trust propagates through a weighted attestation graph by bounded random walks: after t steps, a node’s influence is governed by the transition matrix and rapidly mixes within well-connected honest regions. A sybil coalition instead occupies a sparse external cut with low conductance φ, so conductance and min-cut transitivity bounds limit probability mass crossing into it, capping aggregate voting weight even when identities multiply. The fable, delta, and knoll labels do not alter this spectral bound.
